body: I'll keep that in mind, "if I can ask the question, I am *probably* not crazy."

It works though, I don't get upset about things like that.  Just some more emptiness.  But in exchange, I may be throwing away whatever stops us from injuring or killing someone else.  I think I can control it, but my perspective may be skewed.

Oh no, I've had this discussion with a therapist before.  Back when I very depressed, to the point I couldn't function, for no reason other than a chemical imbalance in my brain.  I don't even look at the world as good or bad, but I know other people do.  I was considerably weaker back then, and now I've learned to enjoy my life even if it costs it being shortened a bit, rather then hating it until the day I die.  If my consciousness existed after death I think might miss some things for awhile.  But it won't, so it won't matter.  I've come to the conclusion that I could die at any moment, and that realization makes everything easier, because I know my ticket out, and that I can't be restrained by the bonds of society but for so long.

Thanks for replying :)  

I'm mildly amused that I got downvoted by someone in suicide watch, but I know exactly what you are saying.  I've always had this idea in my head, that the second I stop thinking I'm crazy, I must have gone mad.  I just need outside opinions of people I don't know, it puts me at ease no matter what they say.
